note: Weblate service accounts that are AI translators or reviewers (ADR-0160 §1, §4, §10). Each account is tied to one named model. The bundle export uses this to enforce 'an AI-written string needs a reviewer on a different model, or a human': an approval where author and approver are both AI on the same model, or either is a Weblate bot account not listed here, is omitted. Nothing here grants access; Weblate does. Filled in by ut-docs#4366, under CODEOWNERS.

bot-universal-till-ai-reviewer-codex.note: Weblate bot (user id 12). Reviews and approves; never approves legal keys (a human-reviewers member does). The model label is the family; a future translator account must name a different model (ut-docs#4366).

bot-universal-till-bootstrap-approver.note: Weblate bot. NOT an AI review: the owner directed (2026-10-29, ut-docs#4371) that the imported de/es/pt/tr strings are accepted as they are so the bundles can ship, to be re-reviewed later. Approves only strings whose author is a human or the import; never legal keys (a human-reviewers member other than the author does). Retire when the re-review is done.

bot-universal-till-ai-translator-local.note: Weblate bot that saves machine translations made by a local Ollama model through tools/bulk_locale.py (ut-docs#4371). Never approves. Its strings are approved by a different account (the codex reviewer, or the bootstrap approver while the re-review is pending).
